United Nations climate talks are heading into overtime this weekend in Turkey.
Negotiations were supposed to wrap up Friday, but talks have spilled into a third night.
NPR's Rachel Walholz reports differences over fossil fuels are holding up in agreement.
Some countries, they want to come away from this climate summit with an agreement that
explicitly calls on the world to transition away from fossil fuels.
That's because burning coal and oil and natural gas is the primary driver of global warming,
and they want that called out. But other countries, especially big oil producers like
Saudi Arabia and Russia, don't want language that specifically targets fossil fuels.
And so that has become a big sticking point for some countries this year.
Walholz adds the U.S. is not taking part in the talks
after the Trump administration withdrew from the Paris climate agreement.
The administration cited in part that the agreement imposes unfair economic burdens
and undermines U.S. energy independence. About 81 million people are expected to
travel over Thanksgiving week. But in California, where high tides and heavy rains are forecast,
one mayor is urging residents to consider staying home. And PR's Eva Berger has the story.
As Americans set their minds on pumpkin pie and cranberry sauce, the weather is not cooperating.
San Francisco Mayor Daniel Laurie said next week the city is expecting extreme high tides and rain.
I'm going to ask you all to consider not traveling unless it is absolutely essential
starting Monday afternoon and going into Wednesday afternoon.
Two atmospheric rivers, which are long bands of water vapor that dump rain on certain areas,
will hover over northern California and the Pacific Northwest.
On the eastern seaboard, a storm is forecasted to move through the Carolinas into New England.
Meteorologists say during a busy travel week,
any challenging weather can cause delays. Eva Berger, NPR News.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has branded Volodymyr Putin a killer
after President Trump referred to the Russian leader in fond terms this week
and PR's Eleanor Beardsley reports.
In response to a question about Trump referring to Putin as his friend, Zelensky told CNN,
"For us, he's an enemy. And of course, for us, he's a killer."
Trump made the comment as he and Putin met alongside China's Xi Jinping in Shenzhen this week.
Trump continued to talk up his relationship with the Russian dictator
during a press conference at the White House on Friday.
On Thursday night, Russian forces launched a major wave of strikes against Ukraine,
killing at least seven people in Kiev and damaging key bridges across the Nipro River.
Zelensky said Russia had fired more than 400 attack drones
and over 110 missiles during the assault,
which he called one of the largest attacks of the war so far.
You're listening to NPR.
In a world's first, researchers say they've been able to sequence
the entire genome of a humpback whale using its nasal mucus.
So how does one collect whale snot, you ask?
Careful timing. And drones.
The drones have got sterile petri dishes attached to them,
literally velcroed on. And then as that whale comes up and breathes out...
Splatter.
Ecologist Aideen Omani and fellow scientists collected dozens of samples
from humpback whales in northern British Columbia.
And a new study shows they were able to use those snot samples to sequence a whole whale genome,
which can tell scientists a lot about the health of the entire species.
All in a non-invasive, albeit stickier way.
Nate Rott, NPR News.
Rockstar Games reports the latest release in the Grand Theft Auto series
has brought in a record $3.79 billion in the first day of retail sales.
The game launched Thursday, marking the first new installment in the series, in 13 years.
Rockstar reports selling 32.5 million units under pre-release.
The launch of Grand Theft Auto 6 far surpasses the release of GTA 5,
which made $1 billion in the first three days back in 2013.
This latest installment returns to the fictionalized Miami,
focusing on characters Lucia Camido and Jason Duvall.
Early reviews highlight greater emphasis on relationship building.
I'm Linda Kenyon, NPR News in Washington.
